documentation.summary: AI-native coding companies (Cognition/Devin, Vercel/v0, Cursor, Sourcegraph Cody, Amazon Q, Codeium) use a layered evaluation stack combining public benchmark participation (SWE-bench Verified, LiveCodeBench), internal 'golden' benchmark suites held blind to training data, trajectory-based autonomous evaluation at scale, and eval-driven development pipelines (evals-in-CI). Contamination prevention is solved primarily through time-segmented benchmarks and held-out private test splits. Flakiness from non-determinism is managed via parallel trajectory sampling, confidence scoring, and prompt regression suites.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Primary anti-contamination mechanism — evaluate models only on problems tagged with a release date AFTER the model's training cutoff. Makes memorization impossible.
common_patterns.example: LiveCodeBench (ICLR 2025): adds new LeetCode/AtCoder/Codeforces problems monthly. Each model is tested only on problems released after its training cutoff. Detects contamination across GPT-4o, Claude, DeepSeek, Codestral. Dataset: 1,055 problems (May 2023 – April 2025).

common_patterns.pattern: Private test split with cloud submission
common_patterns.when_to_use: Independent verification where the ground-truth tests are never publicly released. Models submit code via API/CLI, receive pass/fail without seeing test inputs.
common_patterns.example: SWE-bench Verified test split is kept private. Submission uses sb-cli (cloud-based evaluation). SWE-bench Pro commercial set covers 18 proprietary repositories under formal partnership agreements. Prevents reverse-engineering of test cases.

common_patterns.pattern: Internal golden benchmark with training exclusion
common_patterns.when_to_use: Company-internal quality gate — a private benchmark suite explicitly excluded from training data. Evaluated post-training to measure true generalization.
common_patterns.example: Cognition 'cognition-golden': Devin's production version achieves 74.2% on this benchmark without ever having seen evaluation tasks during training. Used as primary pre-deployment gate.

common_patterns.pattern: Three-annotator human validation of test tasks
common_patterns.when_to_use: Ensuring evaluation tasks are solvable, well-specified, and have appropriate tests before use. Removes ambiguous or broken problems from the eval set.
common_patterns.example: SWE-bench Verified: 93 software engineers annotated 500 problems, each reviewed by 3 separate annotators. Checks: issue description quality, unit test appropriateness, absence of major problems. Estimated residual error rate: 5-10%.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Preventing the code-generating model from influencing its own evaluation. A separate process — unit test runner, rule-based checker, or a different LLM — evaluates the output.
common_patterns.example: SWE-bench: model generates code changes, then a separate unit test runner evaluates the modified repository. Vercel v0: a separate LLM-grader evaluates output quality at scale, independent of the generating model.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Prevent overall scores from masking per-scenario weaknesses. Separate evaluation across task types: bug fixing, feature addition, documentation, refactoring, multi-file work.
common_patterns.example: arXiv 2602.08915 study found a 29 percentage-point gap between task categories. Cursor excels in fix tasks (80.4% PR acceptance); Claude Code leads in documentation (92.3%) and features (72.6%). Task type is the dominant factor in agent performance.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Provide the agent with the expected failing tests as part of the problem specification. Tests serve as a precise behavioral contract. Measures whether the agent can satisfy a concrete test oracle.
common_patterns.example: Cognition/Devin: standard evaluation success rate was 13.86% on SWE-bench. In TDD mode (final unit tests provided alongside problem statement), success rate rose to 23% on 100 sampled tasks — a 66% relative improvement.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Managing flakiness from non-deterministic AI outputs. Run N independent agent trajectories on the same task; aggregate statistically for reliable pass rates.
common_patterns.example: Cognition spawns arbitrarily many parallel evaluation environments to study the long tail of edge cases. Occasional successes on medium-difficulty tasks are used for trajectory-based learning. Statistical aggregation gives reliable measurement even when individual runs vary.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Continuous quality monitoring — treat AI output quality checks as first-class CI gates, analogous to unit tests. Every model update is verified against a golden set before deployment.
common_patterns.example: Vercel eval-driven development: evals run as part of CI pipeline, checking GenAI outputs (generated code, summaries) against defined criteria using automated checks, human feedback, and LLM-based grading. Refusal and safety evals maintain a 100% pass rate gate.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Measuring distinct coding agent capabilities separately rather than as a single score.
common_patterns.example: LiveCodeBench evaluates: (1) code generation, (2) self-repair (fix broken code), (3) code execution (predict output given code), (4) test output prediction. Isolates each capability dimension.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Reduce the rate of broken outputs delivered to users by adding a second model inference pass that detects and repairs generation errors before delivery.
common_patterns.example: Vercel v0 uses a composite model architecture with an AutoFix pass that attempts to prevent or repair broken code generations mid-stream. Limitation: reduces but does not eliminate broken output — code review and tests remain necessary.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Testing agents that must make multiple coherent decisions over time, not just single-pass code generation. Required for autonomous agents like Devin.
common_patterns.example: SWE-bench Pro (2025): 1,865 problems from 41 actively maintained repositories. Partitioned into public set, held-out set (12 repositories), and commercial set (18 proprietary repositories). Specifically targets tasks requiring multiple coherent engineering decisions.

common_patterns.when_to_use: When multiple AI agents are chained — output of one agent becomes input to the next. Per-agent testing is insufficient; end-to-end integration scenarios are required.
common_patterns.example: Enterprise multi-agent pipelines: when agents chain across multiple services, errors compound. A bad output three steps deep is harder to attribute and fix. Testing must cover agent interaction patterns, not just individual agent behavior.

common_patterns.when_to_use: Detecting model drift — cases where a model update changes behavior on previously stable prompts. Catch before deployment.
common_patterns.example: Maintain a suite of prompts with known expected output characteristics. Run on every model update. A regression in output quality on stable prompts indicates model drift requiring investigation.

gotchas.issue: Benchmark contamination via training set overlap
gotchas.solution: Use time-segmented benchmarks (LiveCodeBench) or held-out private splits (SWE-bench Verified). Never release test tasks publicly before model training cutoff.
gotchas.example: HumanEval is now saturated (frontier models score 93%) partly due to training set contamination. LiveCodeBench was designed explicitly to avoid this.

gotchas.issue: Functional correctness does not imply security or efficiency
gotchas.solution: Evaluate correctness, security, and efficiency as separate dimensions using dual-oracle evaluation. Do not conflate pass@k with code quality.
gotchas.example: More than half of AI-generated code samples contain logical or security flaws even when functionally passing tests. Efficiency gap: Eff@k (~0.45) is far below pass@k (>0.8) — models produce correct but slow code. CWEval and SafeGenBench use behavioral monitors for vulnerabilities in addition to unit tests.

gotchas.issue: AI-generated code introduces more issues than human-written code
gotchas.solution: Treat AI output as draft code requiring human code review, not finished code. Apply the same QA gates as human code plus AI-specific evals.
gotchas.example: AI-generated code introduces 1.7x more total issues than human-written code across production systems (Second Talent, 2026 statistics).

gotchas.solution: Run multiple trajectories per task and aggregate statistically. Use temperature control to reduce variance. Build prompt regression suites and model drift monitoring.
gotchas.example: Agentic testing is sensitive to subtle context changes — a slightly delayed loading state or minor UI shift can cause different agent behavior across runs, failing tests that don't reflect actual bugs.

gotchas.issue: Single-agent evaluation is insufficient for multi-agent pipelines
gotchas.solution: Add end-to-end integration scenario tests that cover agent interaction patterns. A bad output from one agent becomes the input to the next.
gotchas.example: In enterprise multi-agent automation, errors compound through the chain. Per-agent unit-level testing misses cross-agent failure modes.

gotchas.issue: SWE-bench Verified still has a 5-10% error rate
gotchas.solution: Do not treat benchmark results as ground truth. Use multiple benchmarks and triangulate. SWE-bench Pro's commercial set has stronger validation via formal partnerships.
gotchas.example: Even with 3-annotator human review of each problem, an estimated 5-10% of SWE-bench Verified samples remain ambiguous or have issues.

examples.title: Cognition Devin: Evaluation pipeline architecture
examples.description: How Cognition evaluates Devin before production deployment
examples.code:
1. Internal 'cognition-golden' benchmark:
   - Tasks explicitly excluded from training data
   - Current score: 74.2% (production model)
   - Gate: must pass before any deployment

2. Parallel autonomous evaluation environments:
   - Spawn N isolated environments per task
   - Run N trajectories independently
   - Study long-tail edge cases statistically
   - Compute objective reliability metrics

3. Trajectory learning:
   - Identify occasional successes on medium-difficulty tasks
   - Use successful trajectories as learning signal
   - Improves future performance without overfitting

4. TDD mode evaluation:
   - Provide final unit tests with the problem statement
   - Measures: can the agent satisfy a concrete test oracle?
   - Standard: 13.86% success, TDD mode: 23% success

examples.title: Vercel v0: Eval-driven development pipeline
examples.description: How Vercel evaluates AI-generated code quality in CI
examples.code:
Evaluation stack (three layers):
1. Automated code checks
   - Fast, reliable, deterministic
   - Rule-based correctness checks
   - AutoFix pass: second model inference to repair broken generations

2. Human feedback
   - End-user feedback (production signals)
   - Internal reviewer feedback
   - Used to calibrate LLM grader

3. LLM-based grading (at scale)
   - Separate evaluator LLM grades generator LLM output
   - Complex qualitative judgments that rule-based checks cannot make
   - Independent of the generating model

CI gate:
   - Evals run on every model update
   - Golden set of expected output quality criteria
   - Refusal/safety evals: 100% pass rate required
   - Hard gate: deploy blocked if eval regression detected

examples.title: LiveCodeBench: Contamination-free evaluation design
examples.description: How LiveCodeBench prevents test contamination for any model
examples.code:
Problem collection:
   - Sources: LeetCode, AtCoder, Codeforces
   - Problems collected continuously, each tagged with release date
   - v6: 1,055 problems (May 2023 – April 2025)

Contamination prevention:
   - Per-model cutoff enforcement: model with training cutoff T
     is only tested on problems with release_date > T
   - No model can have been trained on its test set
   - Rolling updates ensure benchmark stays current

Detection validation:
   - Successfully detects contamination in: GPT-4o, Claude,
     DeepSeek, Codestral (as shown in paper)

Evaluation scenarios (four):
   1. code_generation: write solution from problem statement
   2. self_repair: fix broken code
   3. code_execution: predict output given code + input
   4. test_output_prediction: predict test pass/fail

examples.title: SWE-bench Verified: Independent verification workflow
examples.description: How SWE-bench achieves independent verification of AI code changes
examples.code:
Problem sourcing:
   - Real GitHub issues from popular repos
   - Issues that human engineers already solved
   - Ground truth: the actual merged fix + its tests

Human validation (3-annotator process):
   - 93 software developers annotated 500 problems
   - Each problem: 3 independent annotators check:
     a. Issue description is well-specified
     b. Unit tests are appropriate for the task
     c. No major evaluation-invalidating problems
   - Residual error rate: 5-10%

Blind evaluation flow:
   1. Model receives: repository + issue description
   2. Model makes code changes (no test access)
   3. Submission via sb-cli to cloud evaluator
   4. Cloud runner executes unit tests on modified repo
   5. Pass/fail returned — model never sees test code

Test isolation:
   - Test split kept private (never publicly released)
   - Cloud submission prevents test-set reverse engineering
   - Model has no access to test inputs during generation
